drug_class: Complement inhibitor (a type of biologic medication)
purpose: Eculizumab-aagh is used to treat certain rare blood disorders where your immune system mistakenly destroys your own red blood cells or causes dangerous blood clots. It is approved for conditions like paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS). It can help prevent serious complications and improve your quality of life.
how_it_works: Your immune system has a part called the 'complement system' that normally helps fight infections, but in some diseases it goes haywire and attacks your own blood cells or blood vessels. This medication blocks a specific protein in that system called C5, stopping the chain reaction that causes the damage. Think of it like turning off a faulty alarm that keeps going off when it shouldn't.
common_side_effects: Headache, runny nose or cold-like symptoms, nausea, back pain, fatigue, and diarrhea are among the most commonly reported side effects. Some people may also experience fever or upper respiratory infections.
warnings: The most serious risk is a life-threatening infection called meningococcal meningitis — this medication weakens part of your immune system. You MUST be vaccinated against meningococcal bacteria before or shortly after starting treatment. Watch for sudden headache, fever, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light and seek emergency care immediately if these occur. This drug comes with a special safety program (REMS program) because of this risk. Tell your doctor about all infections before starting.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion in a clinic or hospital, usually by a nurse. For most adults with PNH, dosing typically starts with weekly infusions for about a month, then every two weeks after that. Your doctor will determine the exact schedule and dose based on your specific condition and body weight. Do not miss doses, as this can cause a dangerous flare of your condition.
